blocks.heading: Dismissal and redundancy
blocks.text: For this syllabus comparison, dismissal concerns the employer ending an individual’s employment for a reason connected to that person, such as stated misconduct or inability to perform, whereas redundancy concerns a role no longer being needed. A redundant worker need not have performed badly: a department can close or technology can remove the job. In wider legal usage, termination categories and protections require precise rules, so the comparison does not establish that any particular termination is lawful. Identify the reason in the case rather than calling every job loss poor performance.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: A fictional workshop removes a packing post after replacing that process with machinery. Separately, it terminates another worker for stated serious misconduct while retaining that post. The removed packing role illustrates redundancy; the individual conduct case illustrates the dismissal distinction. The worker’s personal performance is not the reason the packing role disappears.

blocks.heading: Dismissal
blocks.text: For the syllabus contrast with redundancy, dismissal ends an individual’s employment for a stated reason connected to that worker, such as misconduct or capability. The position may remain and another person may fill it. The concept does not mean that any allegation automatically permits a lawful termination; fair procedure and applicable rules are separate questions beyond this simple comparison.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: A hypothetical employer ends a worker’s employment for stated misconduct but retains the job. The individual reason, rather than disappearance of the role, distinguishes this example from redundancy.

blocks.heading: Redundancy
blocks.text: Redundancy occurs when a role or work is no longer required, so the employee loses that job for an operational reason rather than simply poor personal performance. Closure, falling demand or technology can remove posts. The business may still need to follow appropriate procedures, but the teaching distinction here concerns why the job is lost. A redundant worker can have performed well.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: A fictional workshop removes a manual packing role after installing equipment that performs that process. The job is no longer needed, so this illustrates redundancy. It should not be explained as punishment for the worker’s conduct.

blocks.heading: Keeping the ideas apart
blocks.text:
Explain why a fictional cashier losing a job when a branch closes is different from a worker removed for stated misconduct while that role remains.

Branch closure removes the need for the cashier’s role, illustrating redundancy despite possible good performance. The individual conduct case illustrates dismissal in the syllabus contrast. The cause, rather than the shared result of job loss, distinguishes them; the examples do not establish the lawfulness of either action.
